# Error recovery

## Use when
- An action or load failed and the user can do something about it: submit failed, payment declined, request timed out, connection lost.

## Don't use when
- A single field is invalid. Use the Form pattern (`invalid` plus text).
- The list is simply empty. Use the Empty state pattern.
- A background failure the user does not need to act on. Use a `Toast` (`danger`) with a short Retry action only if it is retryable.

## Decision rules
- Show an in-flow `Alert variant="danger"` with a `title` that states what happened and a `description` that states what to do. Put recovery in the Alert `actions` slot as `Button`s. Do not make it dismissible while the problem is still true.
- Classify the failure first, then choose the primary action:
  - The input or method is the problem (card declined, validation rejected by server): primary action is to change it ("Use a different card"); do not offer a bare "Try again" as primary, retrying the same input will fail again.
  - The request is the problem (timeout, network, 5xx): primary action is "Try again" with the same input; say whether the user has been charged or the action completed when that is uncertain.
  - The user cannot fix it (account locked, service down): primary action is the manual path ("Contact support"); no retry button.
- Always offer one alternate way forward: a secondary `Button variant="outline"` or `ghost` ("Contact support", "Go back").
- Keep everything the user entered. Never clear a form because it failed.
- Retry shows loading on the same Button (`loading`), disables nothing else, and on success replaces the Alert with the normal next state.
- Wording: say what happened, not an error code; no blame; no "Oops"; one idea per sentence. Put the code in smaller muted text only if support needs it.
- A blocking decision that cannot be undone is an `AlertDialog`, not an Alert.

## Components and variants
- `Alert` variant: `danger` · size: `md`
- `Button` variant: `primary`, `outline`, `ghost` · size: `md`
- `Input` variant: `default` · size: `md`
- `Toast` variant: `danger`

## Layout and density
- The Alert sits directly above the content it relates to (above the Pay button, above the list), full width of the content column.
- Recovery buttons inside the Alert use `size="sm"`; the page's own primary action stays where it was.

## Hierarchy and composition
- Failure title → one-sentence cause and next step → actions. Only one Alert per failure; two simultaneous failures stack with the more severe first.
- Keep the failed step on screen (do not navigate away to a dedicated error page unless the whole flow cannot continue).

## Responsive behavior
- Actions wrap under the description on a phone, primary first. Never hide the alternate path behind a menu.

## States
- loading (retrying) · error (shown) · recovered (Alert removed, success state or Toast) · exhausted (after repeated failure: swap to the manual path).
- Distinguish error from empty and from loading in the same view.

## Accessibility
- `Alert variant="danger"` already has `role="alert"`, so it is announced assertively. Do not add a second live region for the same message.
- After a failed submit, focus stays on or returns to the retry or first invalid control; never trap it behind the Alert.
- Colour is not the only signal: the Alert has an icon and a title.

## Anti-patterns
- "Something went wrong" with no cause or action.
- Clearing the form on error.
- Retry as the only option after a decline.
- Error shown only in a Toast that auto-dismisses.
- Dismissible Alert for a condition that still holds.
- A blame-the-user message, or a raw error code as the whole message.

## Example
```tsx
import { Alert } from "@atlas/ui-web/compositions/Alert/Alert"
import { Button } from "@atlas/ui-web/primitives/Button/Button"

type Failure = "declined" | "timeout"

export function PaymentFailure({ kind, retrying, onRetry, onChangeCard, onSupport }:
  { kind: Failure; retrying: boolean; onRetry: () => void; onChangeCard: () => void; onSupport: () => void }) {
  // Declined: the card is the problem, so changing it is primary. Timeout: the request is, so retry is.
  return kind === "declined" ? (
    <Alert variant="danger" title="Your card was declined"
      description="You haven't been charged. Use a different card, or contact your bank."
      actions={<>
        <Button size="sm" variant="primary" onClick={onChangeCard}>Use a different card</Button>
        <Button size="sm" variant="ghost" onClick={onSupport}>Contact support</Button>
      </>} />
  ) : (
    <Alert variant="danger" title="The payment timed out"
      description="We couldn't confirm it went through. Your details are saved; try again in a moment."
      actions={<>
        <Button size="sm" variant="primary" loading={retrying} onClick={onRetry}>Try again</Button>
        <Button size="sm" variant="ghost" onClick={onSupport}>Contact support</Button>
      </>} />
  )
}
```
